guideTitle: The Best Docking Stations for Three Monitors
metaDescription: Running three monitors from a laptop depends on DisplayLink, MST or native support. We compared eight docks on how they reach three displays, resolution, charging and ports.
introParagraphs: Three monitors from one laptop is where docks differ most. Most laptops can't drive three external displays natively over one cable, so docks use one of three routes: DisplayLink software (WAVLINK, Plugable UD-ULTCDL, Anker DL7400), native MST on Windows Thunderbolt laptops (Dell SD25TB4), or two dock displays plus one from the laptop's own port.
DisplayLink works with many laptops, including Macs, but needs a driver and adds processor load. Native routes avoid that but depend on your laptop and, on Mac, often won't reach three.
Resolution matters too: some triple docks run one display at 4K 30Hz and two at 1080p. Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

wavlink-pro-dual-4k-universal.badge: Two Dock Displays Plus Your Laptop's Own
wavlink-pro-dual-4k-universal.summary: A universal DisplayLink dock with dual 4K at 60Hz over USB-C or USB-A.
wavlink-pro-dual-4k-universal.description:
The WAVLINK Pro drives two 4K displays at 60Hz through DisplayLink, not three; the route to a third screen is your laptop's own HDMI or USB-C video port, alongside the dock's two.

It connects over USB-C or USB-A and needs the DisplayLink driver. The listing summary doesn't state charging wattage.
wavlink-pro-dual-4k-universal.bestFor: Laptops, including many base M-series Macs, that natively support only one external display.
wavlink-pro-dual-4k-universal.skipIf: You want all three displays from the dock; the WAVLINK Neo drives three for less.

plugable-triple-display-100w.summary: A USB-C dock with 100W and three displays: one 4K at 30Hz and two 1080p at 60Hz.
plugable-triple-display-100w.description:
The Plugable triple-display dock drives three monitors with 100W charging and six 5Gbps USB ports, and supports Windows, macOS and ChromeOS.

Its display split is one 4K at 30Hz and two 1080p at 60Hz, so it suits three modest monitors better than 4K screens. It isn't Thunderbolt certified.
plugable-triple-display-100w.skipIf: You want three 4K 60Hz displays; the Anker DL7400 offers that.

plugable-13in1-ultcdl.summary: A 13-in-1 DisplayLink dock with triple HDMI, 100W, Ethernet and SD; driver required on Mac.
plugable-13in1-ultcdl.description:
The Plugable UD-ULTCDL uses DisplayLink to drive three HDMI displays, including from Macs that natively support fewer, with 100W charging, a 20W USB-C output, Gigabit Ethernet, an SD reader and four more USB ports.

It needs the DisplayLink driver on Mac, which adds some processor load and is less suited to video playback of protected content or gaming.
plugable-13in1-ultcdl.bestFor: Macs that need more monitors than they support natively.
plugable-13in1-ultcdl.skipIf: Your laptop supports your monitors natively; the Plugable TBT-UDM avoids the driver.

anker-prime-dl7400-triple.summary: A 14-port DisplayLink dock with triple 4K at 60Hz, 140W output and a cooling fan.
anker-prime-dl7400-triple.description:
The Anker Prime DL7400 drives three 4K displays at 60Hz through DisplayLink, which is uncommon, with 140W total output, a built-in cooling fan and a display status indicator.

Anker lists it for Windows laptops with the latest DisplayLink driver installed. It isn't Thunderbolt certified.
anker-prime-dl7400-triple.skipIf: You want triple 4K for less; the WAVLINK Neo lists it at about half the price.

wavlink-12in1-3monitors-neo.summary: A 12-in-1 DisplayLink dock driving three 4K@60Hz displays over HDMI and DisplayPort, with 100W and Ethernet.
wavlink-12in1-3monitors-neo.description:
The WAVLINK Neo drives three displays at 4K 60Hz through DisplayLink, using a mix of HDMI and DisplayPort outputs, and it was the lowest-priced triple-4K dock here at the time of writing.

It adds 100W charging, Gigabit Ethernet and 5Gbps USB ports. Like all DisplayLink docks, it needs a driver and adds some processor load.
wavlink-12in1-3monitors-neo.skipIf: You prefer native output; a Thunderbolt dock with MST on Windows avoids DisplayLink.

plugable-tb4-m4-m5-macbook.summary: A Thunderbolt 4 certified dock with 100W, dual 4K HDMI or single 6K, 6 USB, SD and Gigabit Ethernet.
plugable-tb4-m4-m5-macbook.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM drives displays natively over certified Thunderbolt 4, which avoids DisplayLink's driver and processor load, but it supports two 4K displays or one 6K display, not three.

It's included for Mac users who'd rather run two native displays than three via DisplayLink. It has 100W charging, six USB ports, SD and Ethernet.
plugable-tb4-m4-m5-macbook.bestFor: Mac or Windows Thunderbolt laptops with two monitors.
plugable-tb4-m4-m5-macbook.skipIf: You need three monitors; a DisplayLink dock like the Plugable UD-ULTCDL is required on many Macs.

dell-pro-sd25tb4-4display.badge: Best Native Triple Display on Windows
dell-pro-sd25tb4-4display.summary: Dell's certified Thunderbolt 4 dock with 130W, up to 4 displays, 2.5GbE and Wi-Fi.
dell-pro-sd25tb4-4display.description:
The Dell SD25TB4 supports up to four displays via two DisplayPort 1.4, HDMI 2.1 and two Thunderbolt 4 ports. On a compatible Windows Thunderbolt laptop, it can drive three or more displays natively through MST, without DisplayLink.

It adds 130W charging, 2.5GbE and Wi-Fi. MST isn't supported the same way on macOS, and results depend on your laptop.
dell-pro-sd25tb4-4display.bestFor: Dell Pro laptops, including higher-power models.
dell-pro-sd25tb4-4display.skipIf: You don't use Dell; the Plugable is the brand-neutral choice.

anker-prime-14port-dual4k.summary: A 14-port dock with 160W total output, dual 4K, 10Gbps data, Ethernet and audio; not Thunderbolt certified.
anker-prime-14port-dual4k.description:
The Anker Prime 14-port works from a Thunderbolt 4 port but isn't Thunderbolt certified. It offers 14 ports, 160W total output shared across devices, dual 4K, 10Gbps data, Ethernet and audio.

It costs less than the certified docks at the time of writing. It lacks certified Thunderbolt bandwidth and daisy-chaining.
cons: Laptop charging limited by USB PD
anker-prime-14port-dual4k.bestFor: Many USB peripherals without Thunderbolt devices.
anker-prime-14port-dual4k.skipIf: You want three displays from one dock; the WAVLINK Neo does that.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Pick a route to three displays
buyingCriteria.explanation: DisplayLink, native MST (Windows Thunderbolt), or two dock displays plus the laptop's own port.
Triple 4K@60Hz (WAVLINK Neo, Anker DL7400) differs from 4K@30Hz plus two 1080p (Plugable triple).
The Anker DL7400 lists Windows; the Plugable UD-ULTCDL lists Mac with a driver.
Docks here supply 100W to 140W or more.

faq.q: Can my laptop run three monitors?
faq.a: Natively, many can't over one cable. DisplayLink docks work around that.
Multi-Stream Transport lets one connection drive several displays natively; it's supported on Windows but not the same way on macOS.
For office work, generally yes; it's less suited to gaming or protected video.

faq.q: Can I use the laptop's own port for the third screen?
faq.a: Yes, pairing a dual-display dock with the laptop's HDMI or USB-C video port is a common route.
DisplayLink docks do; Thunderbolt docks generally don't.

bottomLine: For three 4K monitors, the WAVLINK Neo is the value DisplayLink dock and the Anker DL7400 the premium Windows option. On a Mac, the Plugable UD-ULTCDL is the listed route.
On a Windows Thunderbolt laptop, the Dell SD25TB4 can reach three displays natively. Otherwise, pair a dual-4K dock with your laptop's own video port.
